text:
Priya: Heads-up  proposing a "prewarm grace tokens" pattern for new Dedicated tenants. Goal: smooth initial ramp without overcommitting reserved capacity. Draft below.

Ravi: Curious how this differs from onboarding headroom?

Priya: Short: headroom reserves GPU. Prewarm tokens are temporary non-reserved allowance that draw from burst capacity but with a soft contract: tracked, surfaced, and reconciled within X days. Less risk to overall packing.

Nora: Example policy (draft):
```
prewarm_grace:
  enabled: true
  allocation_tokens: 50k_requests
  window_days: 21
  cap_pct_of_pool_burst: 5
  reconcile_mode: "charge-if-exceeded" # options: warn-only | charge-if-exceeded | auto-convert-to-reservation
  visibility: per-tenant-dashboard + billing-export
```

Ben: If reconcile_mode=charge-if-exceeded, we need clear invoices and sales playbook. billing-bot: what does "charge" imply on our billing export schema?

billing-bot: charge-if-exceeded -> post-facto usage line item named "prewarm_oob". Must be enabled per-contract. Default: warn-only.

Ravi: Operationally, cap_pct_of_pool_burst is nice, but how do we prevent burst monopolization if many onboard at once?

Priya: Two mitigations: 1) global circuit-breaker on concurrent prewarms (soft cap), 2) proportional degrade when pool burst > threshold. Also a per-tenant fairshare weight.

Nora: Can we make allocation_tokens variable by customer tier? e.g., startup=20k, standard=50k, enterprise=200k.

Priya: Yes. Proposal: token bands by commitment. Keep defaults conservative.

Ben: Acceptance criteria for experiment:
- No more than 2% increase in tail 99th latency in affected pools during prewarm windows
- Billing exports include prewarm_oob line item with tenant IDs for 100% of events
- UX shows "prewarm usage" on onboarding flow and in Console within 24h

Ravi: Rollout plan idea:
- Phase A: internal alpha (20 accounts) with warn-only & telemetry for 2 weeks
- Phase B: opt-in customers (up to 200) with charge-if-exceeded enabled and a simple invoice template
- Phase C: auto-on for new small tenants with warn-only, monitor 30d, then switch to charge-if-exceeded for repeat overages

Nora: Risk: sales will want to promise prewarm to close deals. We should gate on contract language and add an "explicit prewarm add-on" flag.

Ben: Billing ops: agree. Also need refund policy if we mis-attributed prewarm usage (false positives). Propose dispute window 60 days.

Priya: Engineering notes: capacity-bot, can we throttle prewarm at admission-time without changing packing algorithm? If not, we need an engineering spike.

capacity-bot: Current runtime supports burst throttles by tenant token. Admission-level soft-throttles are on an open PR; hard admission gating requires scheduler changes.

Ravi: If scheduler changes are required, add a perf test matrix: N tenants onboarding concurrently, pool sizes 8g/16g/64g. Measure prewarm OOB impact.

Priya: Product decision proposal: ship experiment with warn-only first, per-tier tokens, circuit-breaker limit 10 concurrent prewarms per pool, reconcile_mode default warn-only. Revisit after 45d with telemetry.

Nora: +1 from me. I'll draft the contract language for explicit prewarm add-on and opt-in checkbox in onboarding flow.

Ben: I'll prepare billing export sample and invoice template. Also open support-runbook for disputed charges.

Ravi: I'll scope the spike for admission gating and perf tests. ETA two sprints.

Priya: Great. Action items: @Nora contract + UX, @Ravi eng spike, @Ben billing + runbook, @Priya coordinate canary. Sync in one week. :white_check_mark:
